@graph.name: LexInfo + OntoLex-Lemon (core, synsem)
description: An ontology of types, values and properties to be used with the OntoLex-Lemon model

@graph.name: lexinfo.owl
@graph.description: Source OWL ontology this schema was converted from

@graph.name: ontolex.owl
@graph.description: Source OWL ontology this schema was converted from

@graph.name: synsem.owl
@graph.description: Source OWL ontology this schema was converted from

@graph.name: Convert OWL ontology to MASP schema crate

@graph.rdfs:label: AdjectivePredicateFrame
@graph.name: adjective predicate frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Note this frame should be used when both attributive and predicative use of the adjective is allowed

@graph.rdfs:label: ArbitraryControl
@graph.name: arbitrary control
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates either the subject or object of the main clause may be the omitted argument of the subclause

@graph.rdfs:label: Control
@graph.name: control
@graph.rdfs:comment: Control indicates how a an argument from a main clause will be utilized in a subclause. This class includes both control structures and raising structures

@graph.rdfs:label: DeclarativeFrame
@graph.name: declarative frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Declarative frames take a clause as an argument, this argument is marker with the declarative conjunction ("that" in English)

@graph.rdfs:label: GerundFrame
@graph.name: gerund frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates one of the arguments is a gerund clause

@graph.rdfs:label: InfinitiveFrame
@graph.name: infinitive frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Infinitive frames take an infinitive clause as an argument

@graph.rdfs:label: InterrogativeFrame
@graph.name: interrogative frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the frame has a subframe indicated with the appropriate interrogative (e.g., "who", "where", "how")

@graph.rdfs:label: InterrogativeInfinitiveFrame
@graph.name: interrogative infinitive frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the frame has an argument that is a clause with both an interrogative and the clause is in the infinitive form

@graph.rdfs:label: ObjectControl
@graph.name: object control
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the object of the main clause is also the (omitted) object of the subclause

@graph.rdfs:label: PrepositionalFrame
@graph.name: prepositional frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Abstract frame for words that take a prepositional phrase as an argument

@graph.rdfs:label: RaisingSubject
@graph.name: raising subject
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the syntactic subject of the main clause is in fact the subject of the subclause. The main clause should then be interpreted as being impersonal.

@graph.rdfs:label: RootMorph
@graph.name: morphological root
@graph.rdfs:comment: A root is the portion of a word that (a) is common to a set of derived or inflected forms, (b) is not further analyzable into meaningful elements, and (c) carries the principle portion of meaning of the words in which it functions (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/root).

@graph.rdfs:label: SententialFrame
@graph.name: sentential frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: Sentential frames take a clause as argument, no conjunction is used and the syntax of the clause is the same as a main clause

@graph.rdfs:label: SimulfixMorph
@graph.name: simulfix
@graph.rdfs:comment: A simulfix is a change or replacement of vowels or consonants (usually vowels) which changes the meaning of a word (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/simulfix). Examples include umlaut in Germanic languages, e.g., in the formation of the English plural feet from the singular foot.

@graph.rdfs:label: StemMorph
@graph.name: morphological stem
@graph.rdfs:comment: A stem is the root or roots of a word, together with any derivational affixes, to which inflectional affixes are added (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/stem). A stem consists minimally of a root, but may be analyzable into a root plus derivational morphemes.

@graph.rdfs:label: SubjectControl
@graph.name: subject control
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the subject of the main clause is the (omitted) subject of the subclause

@graph.rdfs:label: TransfixMorph
@graph.name: transfix
@graph.rdfs:comment: A transfix is a discontinuous affix that disrupts the base to which it is attached. The term is reserved for true single affixes, rather than combinations of an infix with an independent prefix or suffix. (Broselow, E., 2000. Transfixation. In G. Booij, et al. (eds.), Ein internationales Handbuch zur Flexion und Wortbildung. 1. Halbband. Mouton De Gruyter, New York, Berlin, p. 552-557.) Examples include discontinuous affixes inserted into a word root, as in root-and-pattern systems of several Semitic languages, e.g., in the Arabic word kitaba "writing" from the root k-t-b.

@graph.rdfs:label: ZeroMorph
@graph.name: zero morph
@graph.rdfs:comment: A zero morph is a morph, consisting of no phonetic form, that is proposed in some analyses as an allomorph of a morpheme that is ordinarily realized by a morph having some phonetic form (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/zero-morph). Examples include the English plural sheep along with the singular sheep.

@graph.rdfs:label: Affix
@graph.name: affix
@graph.rdfs:comment: An affix is a lexical entry that represents a morpheme (suffix, prefix, infix, circumfix) that is attached to a word stem to form a new word.

@graph.rdfs:label: ConceptSet
@graph.name: concept set
@graph.rdfs:comment: A concept set represents a collection of lexical concepts.

@graph.rdfs:label: Form
@graph.name: form
@graph.rdfs:comment: A form represents one grammatical realization of a lexical entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: LexicalConcept
@graph.name: lexical concept
@graph.rdfs:comment: A lexical concept represents a mental abstraction, concept or unit of thought that embodies the meaning of one or more lexical entries.

@graph.rdfs:label: LexicalEntry
@graph.name: lexical entry
@graph.rdfs:comment: A lexical entry represents a unit of analysis of the lexicon that consists of a set of forms that are grammatically related and a set of base meanings that are associated with all of these forms. Thus, a lexical entry is a word, multiword expression or affix with a single part-of-speech, morphological pattern, etymology and set of senses.

@graph.rdfs:label: LexicalSense
@graph.name: lexical sense
@graph.rdfs:comment: A lexical sense represents the lexical meaning of a lexical entry when interpreted as referring to the corresponding ontology element. A lexical sense thus represents a reification of a pair of a uniquely determined lexical entry and a uniquely determined ontology entity it refers to. A link between a lexical entry and an ontology entity via a Lexical Sense object implies that the lexical entry can be used to refer to the ontology entity in question.

@graph.rdfs:label: MultiWordExpression
@graph.name: multi-word expression
@graph.rdfs:comment: A multiword expression is a lexical entry that consists of two or more words.

@graph.rdfs:label: Word
@graph.name: word
@graph.rdfs:comment: A word is a lexical entry that consists of a single token.

@graph.rdfs:label: OntoMap
@graph.name: ontology mapping
@graph.rdfs:comment: An 'ontology mapping' (OntoMap for short) specifies how a syntactic frame and its syntactic arguments map to a set of concepts and properties in the ontology that together specify the meaning of the syntactic frame.

@graph.rdfs:label: SyntacticArgument
@graph.name: Syntactic Argument
@graph.rdfs:comment: A 'syntactic argument' represents a slot that needs to be filled for a certain syntactic frame to be complete. Syntactic arguments typically realize a certain grammatical function (e.g. subject, direct object, indirect object, prepositional object, etc.).

@graph.rdfs:label: SyntacticFrame
@graph.name: Syntactic Frame
@graph.rdfs:comment: A 'syntactic frame' represents the syntactic behavior of an open class word in terms of the (syntactic) arguments it requires. It essentially describes the so called subcategorization structure of the word in question, in particular the syntactic arguments it requires.

@graph.rdfs:label: abbreviationFor
@graph.name: abbreviation for
@graph.rdfs:comment: A linking element used to identify a relation between an abbreviation and its full or expanded form.

@graph.rdfs:label: acronymFor
@graph.name: acronym for
@graph.rdfs:comment: A linking element used to identify a relation between an acronym and its full or expanded form.

@graph.rdfs:label: animacy
@graph.name: animacy
@graph.rdfs:comment: The characteristic of a word indicating that in a given discourse community, its referent is considered to be alive or to possess a quality of volition or consciousness.

@graph.rdfs:label: antonym
@graph.name: antonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: A term or lexeme whose concept or sense constitutes the opposite of the concept represented by a second term or lexeme.

@graph.rdfs:label: approximate
@graph.name: approximate
@graph.rdfs:comment: Property used to qualify something similar but not exactly the same

@graph.rdfs:label: approximateSynonym
@graph.name: approximate synonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: A synonym that differs in some minor way

@graph.rdfs:label: aspect
@graph.name: aspect
@graph.rdfs:comment: Category associated to verbs and referring to the way the grammar marks the duration or type of temporal activity.

@graph.rdfs:label: associativeRelation
@graph.name: associative relation
@graph.rdfs:comment: A relation between two concepts having a non-hierarchical thematic connection by virtue of experience.

@graph.rdfs:label: attitude
@graph.name: attitude
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the speaker’s subjective point of view, positive or negative, regarding the object referred to by a given lexical unit

@graph.rdfs:label: case
@graph.name: case
@graph.rdfs:comment: In a given sentence, the way in which the form of a word changes in order to express a relationship with one or several words of the sentence. The morphological modification may apply to nouns, pronouns noun phrase constituents, such as adjectives or numerals.

@graph.rdfs:label: causallyRelatedConcept
@graph.name: causally related concept
@graph.rdfs:comment: A concept that is related to another concept by virtue of the fact that it plays a causative role with respect to that concept.

@graph.rdfs:label: clippedTermFor
@graph.name: clipped term for
@graph.rdfs:comment: A linking element used to identify a relation between a clipped term and its full or expanded form.

@graph.rdfs:label: cliticness
@graph.name: cliticness
@graph.rdfs:comment: Categorization of the different types of clitics

@graph.rdfs:label: collocation
@graph.name: collocation
@graph.rdfs:comment: Two terms that occur together far more frequently than chance

@graph.rdfs:label: complement
@graph.name: complement
@graph.rdfs:comment: A noun phrase that follows a copula or similar verb, as for example an idiot in the sentence He is an idiot. - A clause that serves as the subject or direct object of a verb or the direct object of a preposition, as for example that he would be early in the sentence I hoped that he would be early

@graph.rdfs:label: confidence
@graph.name: confidence
@graph.rdfs:comment: The confidence in a given relationship.

@graph.rdfs:label: contractionFor
@graph.name: contraction for
@graph.rdfs:comment: The full form that corresponds to a contracted form.

@graph.rdfs:label: coordinateConcept
@graph.name: coordinate concept
@graph.rdfs:comment: A subordinate concept having the same nearest superordinate concept and same criterion of subdivision as some other concept in a given concept system.

@graph.rdfs:label: copulativeArg
@graph.name: copulative arg
@graph.rdfs:comment:
Used with copula constructions. This represents the subject/object in a copula construction. As such constructions are reversible this property is used instead of the usual verb subject/object. E,g.,

Barack Obama is the president/The president is Barack Obama

@graph.rdfs:label: copulativeSubject
@graph.name: copulative subject
@graph.rdfs:comment:
Indicates the subject of a copula construction. It is assumed that by using this the copula construction is not reversible e.g.,

He is happy/*happy is him

@graph.rdfs:label: dating
@graph.name: dating
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indication specifying whether the usage is old or modern.

@graph.rdfs:label: definiteness
@graph.name: definiteness
@graph.rdfs:comment: Property about the possiblity to identify an entity.

@graph.rdfs:label: degree
@graph.name: degree
@graph.rdfs:comment: Property concerning comparison.

@graph.rdfs:label: derivedForm
@graph.name: derived form
@graph.rdfs:comment: A form that is derived morphosyntactically from another form

@graph.rdfs:label: description
@graph.name: description
@graph.rdfs:comment: A description in general prose text of the issues that are indicated by the context. The description field can occur at many different places in a component and profile.

@graph.rdfs:label: directObject
@graph.name: direct object
@graph.rdfs:comment: relation between a phrase and a verb, in which the relation is central to the verb

@graph.rdfs:label: domain
@graph.name: domain
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the specialized field of knowledge in which a lexical unit is mainly used

@graph.rdfs:label: etymologicalRoot
@graph.name: etymological root
@graph.rdfs:comment: Morpheme that has a particular status with regards to the word's etymology.

@graph.rdfs:label: etymology
@graph.name: etymology
@graph.rdfs:comment: Information on the origin of a word and the development of its meaning.

@graph.rdfs:label: exact
@graph.name: exact
@graph.rdfs:comment: Completely equal in every detail

@graph.rdfs:label: explanation
@graph.name: explanation
@graph.rdfs:comment: A statement that describes and clarifies a concept and makes it understandable, but does not necessarily differentiate it from other concepts.

@graph.rdfs:label: finiteness
@graph.name: finiteness
@graph.rdfs:comment: Property referring to finite and non-finite status of a verbal form.

@graph.rdfs:label: frequency
@graph.name: frequency
@graph.rdfs:comment: The relative commonness with which a term occurs.

@graph.rdfs:label: frequencyUsage
@graph.name: frequency usage
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the relative rate of occurrence of a lexical unit in a given textual context

@graph.rdfs:label: fullFormFor
@graph.name: full form for
@graph.rdfs:comment: A linking element used to identify a relation between any full form of a term or lexical unit and its abbreviated form.

@graph.rdfs:label: gender
@graph.name: gender
@graph.rdfs:comment: A grammatical category that indicates grammatical relationships between words in sentences.

@graph.rdfs:label: geographic
@graph.name: geographic
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the place or region where a lexical unit is mainly used

@graph.rdfs:label: geographicalVariant
@graph.name: geographical variant
@graph.rdfs:comment: Description of a specific form used in a certain region as opposed to another form used in another region

@graph.rdfs:label: gloss
@graph.name: gloss
@graph.rdfs:comment:
In TEI: A phrase or word used to provide a gloss or definition for some other word or phrase.
In 1951: Any editorial comment.

@graph.rdfs:label: head
@graph.name: head
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the head element of a phrase

@graph.rdfs:label: hint
@graph.name: hint
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which cannot be classified otherwise

@graph.rdfs:label: holonymTerm
@graph.name: holonym term
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates that the referenced element is a part of this object

@graph.rdfs:label: homograph
@graph.name: homograph
@graph.rdfs:comment: A word that is spelled like another, but that has a different pronunciation, meaning, and/or origin. // Word that is written like another, but that has a different pronunciation, meaning, and/or origin.

@graph.rdfs:label: homonym
@graph.name: homonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: A word that is pronounced like another word and that can be spelled the same way (homograph) or can merely sound the same (homophone). // Word that sounds the same and is written the same as another word but is different in meaning.

@graph.rdfs:label: homophone
@graph.name: homophone
@graph.rdfs:comment: A word that is pronounced in the same way as another word but that is spelled differently. // Word that sounds like another word, but is different in writiing or meaning.

@graph.rdfs:label: hypernym
@graph.name: hypernym
@graph.rdfs:comment: A term with a broader meaning

@graph.rdfs:label: hyponym
@graph.name: hyponym
@graph.rdfs:comment: A term with a narrower meaning

@graph.rdfs:label: indirectObject
@graph.name: indirect object
@graph.rdfs:comment: An indirect object is a grammatical relation that is one means of expressing the semantic role of goal and other similar roles. It is proposed for languages in which the role is distinct from the direct object and the oblique object on the basis of multiple independent syntactic or morphological criteria, such as the following: - Having a particular case marking, commonly dative - Governing an agreement affix on the verb, such as person or number - Being distinct from oblique relations in that it may be relativized

@graph.rdfs:label: initialismFor
@graph.name: initialism for
@graph.rdfs:comment: A linking element used to identify a relation between an initialism and its full or expanded form.

@graph.rdfs:label: meaningType
@graph.name: meaning type
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies a semantic extension of the sense of a given lexical unit

@graph.rdfs:label: memberHolonym
@graph.name: member holonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the object is a member of this

@graph.rdfs:label: memberMeronym
@graph.name: member meronym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates this is an element of the other

@graph.rdfs:label: meronymTerm
@graph.name: meronym term
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates this is a part of another concept

@graph.rdfs:label: modificationType
@graph.name: modification type
@graph.rdfs:comment: Refers to the prenominal or postnominal positions of determiners which distinguish different forms.

@graph.rdfs:label: mood
@graph.name: mood
@graph.rdfs:comment: In TEI: contains information about the grammatical mood of verbs (e.g. indicative, subjunctive, imperative).

@graph.rdfs:label: negative
@graph.name: negative
@graph.rdfs:comment: denotes the negation or the absence

@graph.rdfs:label: normativeAuthorization
@graph.name: normative authorization
@graph.rdfs:comment: A term status qualifier assigned by an authoritative body, such as a standards body or a governmental entity with a regulatory function.

@graph.rdfs:label: normativity
@graph.name: normativity
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the use of a given lexical unit which is in some aspect considered to be non-standard or incorrect

@graph.rdfs:label: note
@graph.name: note
@graph.rdfs:comment: A statement that provides further information on any part of a language resource entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: number
@graph.name: number
@graph.rdfs:comment: Grammatical category for the variation in form of nouns, pronouns, and any words agreeing with them, depending on how many persons or things are referred to. // In many languages, the grammatical distinction that indicates the number of objects referred to by the term or word.

@graph.rdfs:label: partHolonym
@graph.name: part holonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates a part of this object

@graph.rdfs:label: partMeronym
@graph.name: part meronym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates this a component of the other concept

@graph.rdfs:label: partOfSpeech
@graph.name: part of speech
@graph.rdfs:comment: A category assigned to a word based on its grammatical and semantic properties. // Term used to describe how a particular word is used in a sentence.

@graph.rdfs:label: participleFormOf
@graph.name: participle form of
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates that one lexical entry is the participle form of another, e.g., the adjective 'reassuring' is the participle of 'to reassure'

@graph.rdfs:label: partitiveRelation
@graph.name: partitive relation
@graph.rdfs:comment: A relation between two concepts where one of the concepts constitutes the whole and the other concept a part of that whole.

@graph.rdfs:label: person
@graph.name: person
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indication of grammatical person (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.) associated with a given inflected form.

@graph.rdfs:label: pertainsTo
@graph.name: pertains to
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates that a term is the adjectival form of a word with a meaning of 'of or pertaining to X'

@graph.rdfs:label: postPositiveArg
@graph.name: post positive arg
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates an argument of an adjective indicated by post-positive modification. An example in english would be that "that is something interesting", where the adjective interesting post-postively modifies something

@graph.rdfs:label: pronunciation
@graph.name: pronunciation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The representation of the manner by which a term or word is articulated.

@graph.rdfs:label: quasiEquivalent
@graph.name: quasi equivalent
@graph.rdfs:comment: A term that is very similar but with some differences

@graph.rdfs:label: referentType
@graph.name: referent type
@graph.rdfs:comment: Type of concrete object or concept (the referent) that an expression represents (the reference).

@graph.rdfs:label: register
@graph.name: register
@graph.rdfs:comment: Classification indicating the relative level of language individually assigned to a lexeme or term or to a text type.

@graph.rdfs:label: relatedTerm
@graph.name: related term
@graph.rdfs:comment: A term connected to another term by a coordinate or associative relation.

@graph.rdfs:label: romanization
@graph.name: romanization
@graph.rdfs:comment: Transcription or transliteration from non-Latin script into Latin script.

@graph.rdfs:label: root
@graph.name: root
@graph.rdfs:comment: base of a word

@graph.rdfs:label: segmentation
@graph.name: segmentation
@graph.rdfs:comment: Specification of the pointers in time or sequence that indicates the segmentation process.

@graph.rdfs:label: senseExample
@graph.name: sense example
@graph.rdfs:comment: Descriptive material that provides a sample of an object or entity defined in the entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: senseTranslation
@graph.name: sense translation
@graph.rdfs:comment: A label for this sense in another language

@graph.rdfs:label: shortFormFor
@graph.name: short form for
@graph.rdfs:comment: A linking element used to identify a relation between a short form and its full or expanded form.

@graph.rdfs:label: socioCultural
@graph.name: socio cultural
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the use of a given lexical unit by particular social groups and/or in certain types of communicative situations depending on their level of formality

@graph.rdfs:label: subject
@graph.name: subject
@graph.rdfs:comment: relation between a phrase and a verb, that represents the person or thing that performs the action or about which something is stated

@graph.rdfs:label: substanceHolonym
@graph.name: substance holonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates what this is composed of

@graph.rdfs:label: substanceMeronym
@graph.name: substance meronym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates this is a substance that composes the other

@graph.rdfs:label: synonym
@graph.name: synonym
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the the terms have the same meaning lexicographically

@graph.rdfs:label: temporalQualifier
@graph.name: temporal qualifier
@graph.rdfs:comment: An attribution of a term or lexeme with respect to its use over time.

@graph.rdfs:label: tense
@graph.name: tense
@graph.rdfs:comment: Property referring to the way the grammar marks the time at which the action denoted by the verb took place.

@graph.rdfs:label: termElement
@graph.name: term element
@graph.rdfs:comment: Any logically significant portion of a larger term or lexeme.

@graph.rdfs:label: termType
@graph.name: term type
@graph.rdfs:comment: An attribute assigned to a lexeme or a term.

@graph.rdfs:label: textType
@graph.name: text type
@graph.rdfs:comment: usage marker which identifies the typical use of a lexical unit in a particular discourse type or genre

@graph.rdfs:label: translation
@graph.name: translation
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates that two terms are translations of one another; this is the same as interlingual synonymy

@graph.rdfs:label: translationConfidence
@graph.name: translation confidence
@graph.rdfs:comment: The confidence in a given translation.

@graph.rdfs:label: transliteration
@graph.name: transliteration
@graph.rdfs:comment: Form resulting from the conversion of one writing system into another

@graph.rdfs:label: usageNote
@graph.name: usage note
@graph.rdfs:comment: A note containing information on the usage of the associated word or term.

@graph.rdfs:label: verbFormMood
@graph.name: verb form mood
@graph.rdfs:comment: One of a set of distinctive forms that are used to signal modality. Modality is a facet of illocutionary point or general intent of a speaker, or a speaker's degree of commitment to the expressed proposition's believability, obligatoriness, desirability or reality.

@graph.rdfs:label: voice
@graph.name: voice
@graph.rdfs:comment: Way sentences may alter the relationship between the subject and object of a verb, without changing the meaning of the sentence.

@graph.rdfs:label: canonicalForm
@graph.name: canonical form
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'canonical form' property relates a lexical entry to its canoncical or dictionary form. This usually indicates the "lemma" form of a lexical entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: concept
@graph.name: concept
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'concept' property relates an ontological entity to a lexical concept that represents the corresponding meaning.

@graph.rdfs:label: denotes
@graph.name: denotes
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'denotes' property relates a lexical entry to a predicate in a given ontology that represents its meaning and has some denotational or model-theoretic semantics.

@graph.rdfs:label: evokes
@graph.name: evokes
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'evokes' property relates a lexical entry to one of the lexical concepts it evokes, i.e. the mental concept that speakers of a language might associate when hearing the lexical entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: isConceptOf
@graph.name: is concept of
@graph.rdfs:comment: This property formalizes the meaning of a Lexical Concept by linking it to a particular ontological meaning.

@graph.rdfs:label: isDenotedBy
@graph.name: is denoted by
@graph.rdfs:comment: The object property isDenotedBy is the inverse of the object property denotes.

@graph.rdfs:label: isEvokedBy
@graph.name: is evoked by
@graph.rdfs:comment: The inverse relation to evokes.

@graph.rdfs:label: isLexicalizedSenseOf
@graph.name: is lexicalized sense of
@graph.rdfs:comment: The object property isLexicalizedSenseOf is the inverse property of lexicalized sense.

@graph.rdfs:label: isReferenceOf
@graph.name: is reference of
@graph.rdfs:comment: The object property isReferenceOf is the inverse property of reference.

@graph.rdfs:label: isSenseOf
@graph.name: is sense of
@graph.rdfs:comment: The property isSenseOf is the inverse property of sense.

@graph.rdfs:label: lexicalForm
@graph.name: lexical form
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'lexical form' property relates a lexical entry to one grammatical form variant of the lexical entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: lexicalizedSense
@graph.name: lexicalized sense
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'lexicalized sense' property relates a lexical concept to a corresponding lexical sense that lexicalizes the concept.

@graph.rdfs:label: morphologicalPattern
@graph.name: morphological pattern
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'morphological pattern' property indicates the morphological class of a word.

@graph.rdfs:label: otherForm
@graph.name: other form
@graph.rdfs:comment: The  'other form' property relates a lexical entry to a non-preferred ("non-lemma") form that realizes the given lexical entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: phoneticRep
@graph.name: phonetic representation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'phonetic representation' property indicates one phonetic representation of the pronunciation of the form using a scheme such as the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA).

@graph.rdfs:label: reference
@graph.name: reference
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'reference' property relates a lexical sense to an ontological predicate that represents the denotation of the corresponding lexical entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: representation
@graph.name: representation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'representation' property indicates a string by which the form is represented according to some orthography.

@graph.rdfs:label: sense
@graph.name: sense
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'sense' property relates a lexical entry to one of its lexical senses.

@graph.rdfs:label: usage
@graph.name: usage
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'usage' property indicates usage conditions or pragmatic implications when using the lexical entry to refer to the given ontological meaning.

@graph.rdfs:label: writtenRep
@graph.name: written representation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'written representation' property indicates the written representation of a form.

@graph.rdfs:label: condition
@graph.name: condition
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'condition' property defines an evaluable constraint that derives from using a certain lexical entry to express a given ontological predicate.

@graph.rdfs:label: isA
@graph.name: instansie van
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'is a' property represents the single argument of a class or unary  predicate.

@graph.rdfs:label: marker
@graph.name: marker
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'marker' property indicates the marker of a syntactic argument; this can be a case marker or some other lexical entry such as a preposition or particle.

@graph.rdfs:label: objOfProp
@graph.name: object of property
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'objOfProp' represents the 2nd argument or object of a binary predicate (property) in the ontology.

@graph.rdfs:label: ontoCorrespondence
@graph.name: ontological correspondence
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'ontoCorrespondence' property binds an argument of a predicate defined in the ontology to a syntactic argument that realizes this predicate argument syntactically.

@graph.rdfs:label: ontoMapping
@graph.name: Ontologieabbildung
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'ontoMapping'  property relates an ontology mapping to its corresponding lexical sense.

@graph.rdfs:label: optional
@graph.name: optional
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'optional' property indicates whether a syntactic argument is optional, that is, it can be syntactically omitted.

@graph.rdfs:label: propertyDomain
@graph.name: property domain
@graph.rdfs:comment: 'Property domain' provides a pragmatic restriction on the domain of the property referred to by this sense.

@graph.rdfs:label: propertyRange
@graph.name: property range
@graph.rdfs:comment: 'Property domain' provides a pragmatic restriction on the range of the property referred to by this sense.

@graph.rdfs:label: subjOfProp
@graph.name: subject of property
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'subjOfProp' property represents the 1st argument or subject of a binary predicate (property) in the ontology.

@graph.rdfs:label: submap
@graph.name: submap
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'submap' property relates a (complex) ontological mapping to a set of bindings that together bind the arguments of the involved predicates to a set of syntactic arguments that realize them syntactically.

@graph.rdfs:label: synArg
@graph.name: syntactic argument
@graph.rdfs:comment: The object property synArg relates a syntactic frame to one of its syntactic arguments.

@graph.rdfs:label: synBehavior
@graph.name: syntactic behavior
@graph.rdfs:comment: The 'syntactic behavior' property relates a lexical entry to one of its syntactic behaviors as captured by a syntactic frame.

@graph.name: cjk_compound
@graph.description: A lexical unit in a CJKV language that is represented by at least two CJKV characters.

@graph.name: abbreviated form
@graph.description: A term or lexeme resulting from the omission of any part of the full term or lexeme while designating the same concept.

@graph.name: abessive case
@graph.description: Case that expresses the lack or absence of the referent of the noun it marks.

@graph.name: ablative case
@graph.description: Case used to typically indicate locative or instrumental function.

@graph.name: absolutive case
@graph.description: Case for nouns in ergative-absolute languages that would generally be the subjects of intransitive verbs or the objects of transitive verbs in the translational equivalents of nominative-accusative languages such as English.

@graph.name: accusative case
@graph.description: Case used to indicate direct object.

@graph.name: acronym
@graph.description: An abbreviation made up of the initial letters of the components of the full form of the designation or from syllables of the full form and pronounced syllabically.

@graph.name: active voice
@graph.description: Value that expresses the situation where the grammatical subject is also the semantic actor of the verb.

@graph.name: adessive case
@graph.description: Case which expresses the meaning of presence 'at' or 'near' a place.

@graph.name: aditive case
@graph.description: Case expressing "to" in Basque studies.

@graph.name: adjective
@graph.description: Part of speech related to attributes of noun.

@graph.name: adjective-i
@graph.description: Deverbal adjective in Japanese ending with the '-i' suffix in dictionary form

@graph.name: adjective-na
@graph.description: Denominal adjectives in Japanese formed from a noun plus the particle 'na'

@graph.name: admitted term
@graph.description: A term rated according to the scale of a term acceptability rating as a synonym for a preferred term.

@graph.name: adposition
@graph.description: Part of speech that occurs before/inside/after a complement composed of a noun phrase, noun, pronoun or clause that functions as a noun phrase and form a single structure with the complement to express its grammatical and semantic relation to another unit.

@graph.name: adverb
@graph.description: Part of speech to refer to an heterogeneous group of words whose most frequent function is to specify the mode of action of the verb.

@graph.name: affirmative particle
@graph.description: Particle used to express affirmation.

@graph.name: affixed personal pronoun
@graph.description: Personnal pronoun that is affixed, i.e. added as an affix to another word.

@graph.name: allative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses the meaning of motion 'to' or 'towards' the referent it marks.

@graph.name: allusive pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun that refers to something characterized by allusions.

@graph.name: animate
@graph.description: Perceived as alive.

@graph.name: appellation
@graph.description: A designation that represents an individual concept.

@graph.name: archaic form
@graph.description: A term or lexeme no longer in ordinary use, though retained for special purposes.

@graph.name: article
@graph.description: Term used in the grammatical classification of words referring to a subclass of determiners which displays a primary role in differentiating the uses of nouns.

@graph.name: auxiliary
@graph.description: a verb that adds functional or grammatical meaning to the clause in which it appears, so as to express tense, aspect, modality, voice, emphasis, etc.

@graph.name: base element
@graph.description: The root form of a word or term that is used as the formal dictionary entry for the term.

@graph.name: bench level register
@graph.description: Register of terms used in applications-oriented as opposed to theoretical or academic levels of language. // The register of terms used in applications-oriented as opposed to theoretical or academic levels of language.

@graph.name: benefactive case
@graph.description: Case that expresses that the referent of the noun it marks receives the benefit of the situation expressed by the clause.

@graph.name: bound
@graph.description: Linked to a particular element.

@graph.name: bullet
@graph.description: Sign used to mark an item in a list.

@graph.name: cardinal numeral
@graph.description: A word denoting a number.

@graph.name: causative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses that the referent of the noun it marks is the cause of the situation expressed by the clause.

@graph.name: cessative
@graph.description: Aspect that expresses the cessation of an event or state.

@graph.name: circumposition
@graph.description: Adposition which consists of two parts which are positioned ahead and after the adpositional foci.

@graph.name: clipped term
@graph.description: An abbreviation formed by truncating a part of a simple term.

@graph.name: close parenthesis
@graph.description: End of a parenthesis pair.

@graph.name: collective
@graph.description: A collective number is a number referring to 'a set of things'. Languages that have this feature can use it to get a phrase like 'flock of sheeps' by using 'sheep' in collective number.

@graph.name: collective pronoun
@graph.description: A pronoun that refers to all elements of a set.

@graph.name: colon
@graph.description: Sign with two vertical points that is used in writing and printing to introduce an explanation, example or quotation.

@graph.name: comitative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses a meaning similar to 'along with' or 'accompagnied by'.

@graph.name: comma
@graph.description: Mark (,) used in writing to show a short pause or to separate items in a list.

@graph.name: common gender
@graph.description: Indistinguished gender for epicenes.

@graph.name: common name
@graph.description: A synonym for an international scientific term that is used in general discourse in a given language.

@graph.name: common noun
@graph.description: A noun or adjective denoting a class of objects. // Noun that signifies a non-specific member of a group.

@graph.name: commonly used
@graph.description: Said of a term that appears frequently.

@graph.name: comparative
@graph.description: Comparative is the comparison where only two entites are involved.

@graph.name: comparative particle
@graph.description: Particle used to compare.

@graph.name: compound
@graph.description: A lexical unit that combines two or sometimes more different words, frequently such that the sense of the new lexical unit is not clearly derivable from the combination of its parts.

@graph.name: compound preposition
@graph.description: Preposition that is a aggregation of words

@graph.name: conditional
@graph.description: A conditional relation is a logical relation in which the illocutionary act employing one of a pair of propositions is expressed or implied to be true or in force if the other proposition is true.

@graph.name: conditional particle
@graph.description: conditional particule

@graph.name: conditional pronoun
@graph.description: conditional pronoun

@graph.name: conjunction
@graph.description: Word that syntactically links words or constituents, and expresses a semantic relationship between them.

@graph.name: contraction
@graph.description: A lexical unit formed by a shortening of a word, syllable, or word group by omission of a sound or letter.

@graph.name: coordinating conjunction
@graph.description: Conjunction that links constituents.

@graph.name: coordination particle
@graph.description: particle for coordination

@graph.name: copula
@graph.description: Special word that combines the subject of a sentence and its description.

@graph.name: dative case
@graph.description: Case that expresses an indirect object relationship or a range of meaning similar to that covered by 'to' or 'for' in English; but there is a great deal of variation between languages in the way this case is used.

@graph.name: deficient verb
@graph.description: verb lacking certain morphosyntactic properties

@graph.name: definite
@graph.description: Value referring to the capacity of identification of an entity.

@graph.name: definite article
@graph.description: Article that allows the reference to a specific, identifiable entity (or class of entities).

@graph.name: delative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses motion downward from the referent of the noun it marks.

@graph.name: demonstrative determiner
@graph.description: Determiner used to point to an entity in the situation or elsewhere in a sentence.

@graph.name: demonstrative pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun used to point to an entity in the situation or elsewhere in a sentence.

@graph.name: deprecated term
@graph.description: A term rated according to the scale of a term acceptability rating as undesired.

@graph.name: determiner
@graph.description: Word or affix that belongs to a class of noun modifiers that expresses the reference, including quantity, of a noun.

@graph.name: diminutive noun
@graph.description: diminutive noun

@graph.name: direct case
@graph.description: An unmarked case which covers the single argument of a one-place verb and the agent and patient arguments of a transitive verb.

@graph.name: distinctive particle
@graph.description: distinctive particle

@graph.name: dual
@graph.description: Form used in some languages to designate two persons or things. // The form used in some languages to designate two persons or things.

@graph.name: elative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses the meaning of motion 'away from' from the referent of the noun it marks.

@graph.name: emphatic pronoun
@graph.description: An emphatic pronoun is a personal pronoun that is used to emphasize its referent.

@graph.name: entry term
@graph.description: A term that heads a terminological entry.

@graph.name: equation
@graph.description: An expression used to represent a concept based on a statement that two mathematical expressions are, for instance, equal as identified by the equal sign (=), or assigned to one another by a similar sign.

@graph.name: equative case
@graph.description: Case that expresses likeness or identity to the referent of the noun it marks. It can have meaning, such as: 'as', 'like', or 'in the capacity of'.

@graph.name: ergative case
@graph.description: Case assigned to the subject of a transitive verb as opposed to absolutive case.

@graph.name: essive case
@graph.description: Case which expresses a state of being.

@graph.name: exclamative determiner
@graph.description: Determiner expressing an emotional utterance and marked with a strong intonation.

@graph.name: exclamative point
@graph.description: Special sign (!) usually used in writing to mark exclamation.

@graph.name: exclamative pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun marked with an emotional utterance and/or a strong intonation.

@graph.name: existential pronoun
@graph.description: pronoun that indicates the existence of something or someone

@graph.name: expression
@graph.description: A significant word or phrase.

@graph.name: feminine
@graph.description: Of, relating to, or constituting the gender that ordinarily includes most words or grammatical forms referring to females.

@graph.name: finite
@graph.description: Property applied to a verb form that can occur on its own in an independent sentence.

@graph.name: first person
@graph.description: First person deixis is deictic reference that refers to the speaker, or both the speaker and referents grouped with the speaker

@graph.name: formula
@graph.description: Figures, symbols or the like used to express a concept briefly, such as a mathematical or chemical formula.

@graph.name: full article
@graph.description: For definiteness, when a specific form is the syntactic subject of the clause.

@graph.name: full form
@graph.description: The complete presentation of a term or lexeme for which there is an abbreviated form.

@graph.name: fused preposition
@graph.description: Preposition that is the result of a morphological merge from at least two words.

@graph.name: fused preposition determiner
@graph.description: word resulting from the aggregation of a proposition and a determiner

@graph.name: fused preposition pronoun
@graph.description: word resulting from the aggregation of a preposition and a pronoun

@graph.name: fused pronoun auxiliary
@graph.description: word resulting from the aggregation of a pronoun and an auxiliary

@graph.name: future
@graph.description: Verb tense that indicates action or state of being in the future.

@graph.name: future particle
@graph.description: Particle used in order to express future.

@graph.name: general adverb
@graph.description: Adverb belonging to the general class of adverbs

@graph.name: generalization word
@graph.description: A word that does not carry its own meaning but generalizes the meaning of a neighboring word, adding the "etc." sense.

@graph.name: generic numeral
@graph.description: A numeral used to indicate the number of sets/kinds of objects.

@graph.name: genitive case
@graph.description: Case which expresses a possessive relationship (e.g. the boy's book) or some other similarly close connection (e.g. a summer's day).

@graph.name: idiom
@graph.description: A group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word understood on its own.

@graph.name: illative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses the meaning of 'motion into' or 'direction towards' the referent of the noun it marks.

@graph.name: imperative
@graph.description: Mood used to express an order.

@graph.name: imperfect
@graph.description: Verb tense that refers to action in the past that is incomplete or ongoing.

@graph.name: imperfective
@graph.description: Imperfective aspect is an aspect that expresses an event or state, with respect to its internal structure, instead of expressing it as a simple whole.

@graph.name: impersonal pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun lacking person referent.

@graph.name: in house register
@graph.description: Register of terms that are company-specific and not readily recognized outside this environment. // The register of terms that are company-specific and not readily recognized outside this environment.

@graph.name: inanimate
@graph.description: Perceived as not living.

@graph.name: inchoative
@graph.description: Aspect that expresses the beginning of an event or state.

@graph.name: indefinite
@graph.description: Value related to an entity in a situation where the identification of this entity is not clear cut.

@graph.name: indefinite article
@graph.description: Article not capable of expressing identification.

@graph.name: indefinite cardinal numeral
@graph.description: A word used to express imprecise quantity.

@graph.name: indefinite determiner
@graph.description: Determiner not capable of identification.

@graph.name: indefinite multiplicative numeral
@graph.description: A word indicating imprecise number of times something happened.

@graph.name: indefinite ordinal numeral
@graph.description: A word used to indicate imprecise rank of an object in a sequence.

@graph.name: indefinite pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun that does not allow reference.

@graph.name: indicative
@graph.description: Mood value used in the expression of statements and questions.

@graph.name: indifferent
@graph.description: Markup to express that there is not any pertinence.

@graph.name: inessive case
@graph.description: Case which expresses the meaning of location or position within a place.

@graph.name: infinitive
@graph.description: Mood cited as unmarked or base form.

@graph.name: infinitive particle
@graph.description: Particle used to express infinitive.

@graph.name: inflection element
@graph.description: An element of language used to change the form of a word (noun, adjective) by declension, and (verbs) by conjugation.

@graph.name: infrequently used
@graph.description: Said of a term that does not appear frequently.

@graph.name: initialism
@graph.description: An abbreviation made up of the initial letters of the components of the full form of the designation or from syllables of the full form and pronounced letter by letter.

@graph.name: instrumental case
@graph.description: Case indicating that the referent of the noun it marks is the means of the accomplishment of the action expressed by the clause.

@graph.name: interjection
@graph.description: Word or sound that expresses an emotion.

@graph.name: international scientific term
@graph.description: A term that is part of an international scientific nomenclature as adopted by an appropriate scientific body.

@graph.name: internationalism
@graph.description: A term that has the same or nearly identical orthographic or phonemic form in many languages.

@graph.name: interrogative cardinal numeral
@graph.description: An interrogative/relative word used to ask about quantity.

@graph.name: interrogative determiner
@graph.description: Determiner used to express a question.

@graph.name: interrogative multiplicative numeral
@graph.description: An interrogative/relative word used to ask about the number of times something happened.

@graph.name: interrogative ordinal numeral
@graph.description: An interrogative/relative word used to ask about numeric ranking.

@graph.name: interrogative particle
@graph.description: Particle used to express a question.

@graph.name: interrogative pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun used to express a question.

@graph.name: interrogative relative pronoun
@graph.description: pronoun which may act as a relative pronoun or an interrogative one

@graph.name: inverted comma
@graph.description: Inverted comma.

@graph.name: irreflexive personal pronoun
@graph.description: personal pronoun which is not reflexive

@graph.name: lative case
@graph.description: Case which expresses motion to a location.

@graph.name: legal term
@graph.description: A term that is legally defined and used in legally binding documents.

@graph.name: light verb
@graph.description: verb participating in a complex predication that has little semantic content of its own.

@graph.name: locative case
@graph.description: Case that indicates a final location of action or a time of the action.

@graph.name: logical expression
@graph.description: An expression used to represent a concept based on mathematical or logical relations, such as statements of inequality, set relationships, boolean operations, and the like.

@graph.name: main verb
@graph.description: Main verb in contrast to a modal or an auxiliary.

@graph.name: masculine
@graph.description: Of, relating to, or constituting the gender that ordinarily includes most words or grammatical forms referring to males.

@graph.name: mass noun
@graph.description: Designation of a term or word that is not countable and cannot generally be used with the indefinite article or in the plural.

@graph.name: middle voice
@graph.description: Value for middle voice that expresses that the subject is both the agent and object, or that the subject is separate from the agent or that the receiver is the agent him/herself.

@graph.name: modal
@graph.description: Verb form that is usually used with another verb to express ideas such as possibilities, permission, or intention.

@graph.name: modern
@graph.description: Currently in use.

@graph.name: morphological element
@graph.description:
Unit resulting from the division of words into their smallest meaningful parts.
Note: moved to lexeme element from being an independent element; note that this is currently an independent element in 12620

@graph.name: multiplicative numeral
@graph.description: A word that expresses the number of times something happened.

@graph.name: negative particle
@graph.description: Particle used to express negation.

@graph.name: negative pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun used in a context of a negation or for expressing a negation.

@graph.name: neuter
@graph.description: Of, relating to, or constituting the gender that ordinarily includes most words or grammatical forms referring to objects that are not characterized as male or female.

@graph.name: neutral register
@graph.description: The register appropriate to general texts or discourse.

@graph.name: no
@graph.description: Value for negation.

@graph.name: nominative case
@graph.description: Case used to indicate the subject of a verb.

@graph.name: non finite
@graph.description: Property related for verb forms occurring on their own only in dependent clauses and lacking tense and mood contrasts.

@graph.name: noun
@graph.description: Part of speech used to express the name of a person, place, action or thing.

@graph.name: nucleus
@graph.description: The component of a multiword or multi-morphemic compound term that is determined or modified by the other components making up the term.

@graph.name: numeral
@graph.description: Part of speech that expresses a number or the relation to a number.

@graph.name: numeral fraction
@graph.description: Word used to denote the denominator of a fraction.

@graph.name: oblique case
@graph.description: Case that is used when a noun is the object of a verb or a proposition, except for nominative and vocative case.

@graph.name: obsolete form
@graph.description: A term or lexeme which is no longer in common use.

@graph.name: old
@graph.description: Used in the past.

@graph.name: open parenthesis
@graph.description: Beginning of a pair of parenthesis.

@graph.name: optional element
@graph.description:
1951: An optional part of a headword.
1951; examples? The question arises whether these are true options or whether the options reflect synonyms or hyponyms (e.g., barrage, barrage de retenue). The question is not whether 1951 should use this markup, but rather how to map this markup in a global environment.

@graph.name: ordinal adjective
@graph.description: Adjective/numeral/number expressing a numeric ranking.

@graph.name: other animacy
@graph.description: Perceived as related to animacy, but without specific reference to the previous items.

@graph.name: other gender
@graph.description: A grammatical category that indicates grammatical relationships between words in sentences.

@graph.name: other number
@graph.description: Designation used to classify number-related grammatical information that can differ from the standard European classifications cited above.

@graph.name: outdated form
@graph.description: A term or lexeme that has fallen from fashion, but the meaning of which is readily recognizable.

@graph.name: part number
@graph.description: A unique alphanumeric designation assigned to an object in a manufacturing system.

@graph.name: participle
@graph.description: Term referring to a word derived from a verb and used as an adjective.

@graph.name: participle adjective
@graph.description: Adjective based on a verb.

@graph.name: particle
@graph.description: Word that does not belong to one of the main classes of words, is invariable in form, and typically has grammatical or pragmatic meaning.

@graph.name: partitive article
@graph.description: Article expressing a part or quantity.

@graph.name: partitive case
@graph.description: Case that expresses the partial nature of the referent of the noun it marks, as opposed to expressing the whole unit or class of which the referent is a part.

@graph.name: passive voice
@graph.description: Term referring to a situation where the grammatical subject is typically the recipient or goal of the action denoted by the verb.

@graph.name: past
@graph.description: Past tense is an absolute tense that refers to a time before the moment of utterance.

@graph.name: past participle adjective
@graph.description: Adjective based on a past participle.

@graph.name: paucal
@graph.description: Number that specifies 'a few' things.

@graph.name: perfective
@graph.description: Perfective aspect is an aspect that expresses a temporal view of an event or state as a simple whole, apart from the consideration of the internal structure of the time in which it occurs.

@graph.name: personal
@graph.description: Property that refers to the person.

@graph.name: personal pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun referring a person.

@graph.name: phraseological unit
@graph.description: Any group of two or more words that form a unit, the meaning of which frequently cannot be deduced based on the combined sense of the words making up the phrase.

@graph.name: plain verb
@graph.description: verb which has its own semantics

@graph.name: plural
@graph.description: The form of a term or word (usually of a noun) used to designate more than one object. // Value that expresses more than one element.

@graph.name: point
@graph.description: Sign (.) used to expresses the end of a sentence or an abbreviation.

@graph.name: positive
@graph.description: Value used in a comparison relationship when no comparison is involved.

@graph.name: possessive
@graph.description: Relative to the possession or association.

@graph.name: possessive adjective
@graph.description: An adjective derived from a noun and denoting possession by the object described by the noun.

@graph.name: possessive determiner
@graph.description: Determiner that expresses ownership.

@graph.name: possessive particle
@graph.description: Particle expressing ownship.

@graph.name: possessive pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun that expresses ownership and relationships like ownership, such as kinship, and other forms of association.

@graph.name: possessive relative pronoun
@graph.description: A relative pronoun whose antecedent is the possessor of the subject or object in the relative clause.

@graph.name: post modifier
@graph.description: Situation where the modifier is after the modified.

@graph.name: postposition
@graph.description: Adposition that appears at the end of the noun phrase.

@graph.name: pre modifier
@graph.description: Situation where the modifier is before the modified.

@graph.name: preferred term
@graph.description: A term rated according to the scale of a term acceptability rating as the primary term for a given concept.

@graph.name: preposition
@graph.description: Adposition placed at the beginning of a noun phrase.

@graph.name: prepositional adverb
@graph.description: adverb which is very similar in its form to a preposition

@graph.name: present
@graph.description: Verb tense that indicates action or state of being in the present.

@graph.name: present participle adjective
@graph.description: Adjective based on a present participle.

@graph.name: presentative pronoun
@graph.description: pronoun that identify the current locative or temporal situation

@graph.name: preterite
@graph.description: The simple past or preterite as distinct from the perfect form, e.g,, "showed" not "shown"

@graph.name: product name
@graph.description: An attribute assigned to a term indicating that that term is the official designator for a product.

@graph.name: prolative case
@graph.description: Case for a noun or a pronoun that expresses motion within a place or a period of time needed for an event.

@graph.name: pronominal adverb
@graph.description: adverb formed in replacement of a preposition and a pronoun

@graph.name: pronoun
@graph.description: Word used in place of a noun or a noun phrase.

@graph.name: proper noun
@graph.description: A noun or adjective denoting a single object. // Noun that is the name of a specific individual, place, or object.

@graph.name: proverb
@graph.description: A brief popular axiom or saying.

@graph.name: punctuation
@graph.description: Graphical mark used either at word level to indicate an abbreviation or at a text level to separate phrases or sentences.

@graph.name: quadrial
@graph.description: Property related to four elements.

@graph.name: qualifier adjective
@graph.description: Adjective used to qualify.

@graph.name: question mark
@graph.description: Sign used to express a question.

@graph.name: radical
@graph.description: A basic identifiable component of every CJKV character, often found on the left side of the character, that sometimes gives a rough indication of meaning and is used for collating lexical and terminological resources.

@graph.name: rarely used
@graph.description: Said of a term that is almost never used.

@graph.name: reciprocal pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun expressing mutual relationship.

@graph.name: reflexive determiner
@graph.description: Determiner that refers to the same entity.

@graph.name: reflexive personal pronoun
@graph.description: personal pronoun which is reflexive

@graph.name: reflexive possessive pronoun
@graph.description: A possessive pronoun that refers to the subject as the possessor.

@graph.name: regulated term
@graph.description: A term defined by law or government regulation.

@graph.name: relation noun
@graph.description: relation noun

@graph.name: relative determiner
@graph.description: Determiner related to a referent.

@graph.name: relative particle
@graph.description: relative particle

@graph.name: relative pronoun
@graph.description: Pronoun which introduces a relative clause and refers to something that has been said before.

@graph.name: second person
@graph.description: Second person deixis is deictic reference to a person or persons identified as addressee.

@graph.name: semi colon
@graph.description: Sign (;) usually used to separate phrases.

@graph.name: set phrase
@graph.description: A fixed, lexicalized phrase.

@graph.name: short article
@graph.description: For definiteness, when a specific form is not the syntactic subject of the clause.

@graph.name: short form
@graph.description: A variant of a multiword term or lexeme that includes fewer words than the full form.

@graph.name: singular
@graph.description: The form of a term or word (usually of a noun) used to designate one object. // Value that expresses one element.

@graph.name: sku
@graph.description: An inventory item identified by a unique alphanumeric designation assigned to an object in an inventory control system.

@graph.name: slang register
@graph.description: An extremely informal register of a word, term, or text that is used in spoken and everyday language and less commonly in documents.

@graph.name: slash
@graph.description: The punctuation sign /

@graph.name: sociative case
@graph.description: Case related to the person in whose company the action is carried out, or to any belongings of people which take part in the action.

@graph.name: standard text
@graph.description: A fixed chunk of recurring text.

@graph.name: standardized term
@graph.description: A term that has been standardized by a standardizing body.

@graph.name: string
@graph.description: A chunk of text used in a software interface, documentation, help file, or the like.

@graph.name: string category
@graph.description: A type value assigned to a string.

@graph.name: strong personal pronoun
@graph.description: Personal pronoun that can occupy the position after a preposition and/or reinforce a weak personal pronoun.

@graph.name: subjunctive
@graph.description: Mood often used to express uncertainty, whishes or desires.

@graph.name: sublative case
@graph.description: Case for a move of something to the surface of another object.

@graph.name: subordinating conjunction
@graph.description: Conjunction that links constructions by making one of them a constituent of another. The subordinating conjunction typically marks the incorporated constituent.

@graph.name: superessive case
@graph.description: Case indicating location on top of something or on the surface of something.

@graph.name: superlative
@graph.description: Value used in a comparison between more than two entities.

@graph.name: superlative particle
@graph.description: Particle expressing superlative degree. Superlative is the comparison between more than two entities and contrasts with comparative where only two entities are involved and positive where no comparison is implied.

@graph.name: superseded term
@graph.description: A term that is no longer preferred or admitted.

@graph.name: suspension points
@graph.description: Sequence of three dots having the same meaning as "et cetera" (full form) or "etc" (abbreviated form).

@graph.name: syllable
@graph.description: A unit of spoken language that is next bigger than a speech sound and consists of one or more vowel sounds alone or of a syllabic consonant alone or of either with one or more consonant sounds preceding or following.

@graph.name: symbol
@graph.description: A character or glyph representing an idea, concept or object

@graph.name: technical register
@graph.description: The register appropriate to scientific texts or special languages.

@graph.name: terminative case
@graph.description: Case that indicates to what or where something ends.

@graph.name: third person
@graph.description: Third person deixis is deictic reference to a referent(s) not identified as the speaker or addressee.

@graph.name: transcribed form
@graph.description: A form of a term or lexeme resulting from an operation whereby the characters of one writing system are represented by characters from another writing system, taking into account the pronunciation of the characters converted.

@graph.name: translative case
@graph.description: Case indicating that the referent of the noun, or the quality of the adjective, that it marks is the result of a process of change.

@graph.name: trial
@graph.description: Grammatical number referring to 'three things', as opposed to 'singular' and 'plural'.

@graph.name: unaccomplished
@graph.description: aspect that expresses an event or state that is not finished.

@graph.name: unclassified particle
@graph.description: Particle that is not covered by other sorts of particle definitions.

@graph.name: verb
@graph.description: Element which, singly or in combination with other verbs is used as the minimal predicate of a sentence, co-occurring with a subject. If the predicate contains other elements (e.g. object, complement), then it is the verb which more than any other is the unit which influences the choice and extent of these elements.

@graph.name: vocative case
@graph.description: Case used to indicate direct address.

@graph.name: vulgar register
@graph.description: Register of a term or text type that can be characterized as profane or socially unacceptable. // The register of a term or text type that can be characterized as profane or socially unacceptable.

@graph.name: weak personal pronoun
@graph.description: Personal pronoun that cannot occupy the position after a preposition and/or reinforce a strong personal pronoun.

@graph.name: word element
@graph.description: Any lexeme element in a compound lexical unit that is itself a word.

@graph.name: yes
@graph.description: Positive value
